newsitem.title: LESOTHO: Lesotho government steps up privatisation drive.
newsitem.headline: Lesotho government steps up privatisation drive.

text.p: Lesotho's government announced the names on Wednesday of the first 10 enterprises earmarked for sale under a private sector development programme, stepping up its plans for the privatisation of state assets.

The kingdom's privatisation unit told reporters in Maseru it wanted to secure strategic partners particularly for key assets like Lesotho Airways Corporation, Loti Brickworks, Lesotho Pharmaceutical Corporation and Government Mechanical Workshops.

Other enterprises published in the Gazette by the unit, attached to the Ministry of Finance, included the Lesotho Flour Mills and two mountain tourist lodges at Marakabei in the Maseru district and Quthing in southern Lesotho.

In addition, the government wants to sell shares held by the Lesotho National Development Corporation (LNDC) -- its industrial development arm -- in the foodmarket chain OK Bazaars (Lesotho), clothing retailer Smart Centre and building materials retailers Cashbuild.
The privatisation unit said the LNDC shares in these companies would be transferred to a new holding company and sold to the public.
Under the Privatisation Act, the public has 60 days to offer comment on the privatisation. The government's negotiations with prospective investors are then expected to get under way.
Lesotho, a landlocked mountain kingdom, is heavily dependent on the region's economic giant South Africa, which surrounds it.
Most of its trade is with Pretoria and it relies on remittances from miners working in South Africa. Customs receipts make up about half of government revenue.
